artifacts.synopsis: The Mt. Carmel Session complained that New Jersey Presbytery erred by adopting a resolution of Affirmations and Denials Regarding the Interpretation of Genesis One that denied the 24-hour-day view as the only acceptable interpretation. The SJC majority denied the complaint (12-9), holding that NJP acted within its constitutional authority under BCO 11-4 to resolve questions of doctrine, consistent with prior General Assembly decisions allowing latitude on creation-day interpretation; a minority report was filed and the case was referred to the 26th General Assembly for final disposition.

artifacts.title: Hathaway v. Grace Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Vaughn Hathaway complained that the Session of Waynesboro Presbyterian Church refused to furnish him, as pastor and member of the Session, with copies of financial reports the Session had authorized. The panel found Specification 6 sustained (the pastor had a right to the reports as a session member) but declared the complaint moot because Hathaway's pastoral relation had been terminated before the case was decided.

artifacts.title: Meaning and manner of reaffirmation of faith for membership

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that 'reaffirmation of faith' historically means answering BCO 58-5 questions 1 and 2, but a testimony of Christian experience may also satisfy it, and requesting reaffirmation of transferring members is not improper.

artifacts.title: Session oversight of a church lacking a full session

matches.evidence: The CCB directed Rev. Dunkerley to BCO 12-2, noting that church courts have latitude to establish rules not violating the Constitution when a congregation has only one ruling elder and no full session.

artifacts.title: Relationship of assistant pastor to congregation under BCO 22

matches.evidence: An overture detailing how assistant pastors are called was found in conflict with BCO 3-2 and 12-2 through 12-4, as the relationship of an assistant pastor to a congregation is best left to the session.
